messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>

Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — cost qualification & per-1M comparisons

Hi Anjali — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps we agreed on: 

- Volume profile: Lumina expects a phased ramp. For sizing we used a representative mid case of 500M tokens/month and a stretch case up to ~1.2B tokens/month. You indicated the 6–12 month budget window is the priority.
- Target economics: your procurement band is roughly $18k–$45k/month in committed spend (ballpark), which maps to an implied target of ~$18–$40 per 1M tokens depending on caching and peak shaping.
- Primary constraints: SLA, data residency (US only), and auditability for PHI adjacency.

Attached are two artifacts we discussed: a) a 500M-case cost-modeling worksheet (lumina-cost-500M-case.xlsx) and b) a short Redwood vs hosts per-1M comparison (redwood-vs-hosts-1M-comparison.pdf). The comparison uses public host list prices + our optimized serving profiles (includes quantized private variants and caching effects).

High-level per-1M examples (rounded):
- OpenAI (public endpoint, current gen): ~$70–80 / 1M tokens
- Anthropic (public endpoint): ~$60–75 / 1M tokens
- Hosted open-model providers (managed open models): ~$28–45 / 1M tokens (depends on GPU type / quantization)
- Redwood Dedicated / Private (optimized caching + batching): target range $22–35 / 1M tokens for the 500M case; can go lower with KV/prefix caching and committed burst pools.

Key assumptions behind Redwood numbers: 1) persistent KV caching for repeated prefixes, 2) 8-bit quantized runtime for the chosen open model, 3) 99th-percentile latency target of 350ms for first response. The attached workbook shows sensitivity by cache hit rate and throughput.

Next steps we agreed: 
1) I’ll send the 500M-case workbook and a short per-1M scenario that maps to your $/month bands (attached).
2) You’ll confirm whether the legal team needs a draft SOW + SLA before pricing conversations (you flagged procurement review).
3) Schedule a follow-up with procurement + engineering to walk the 500M-case on Friday (May 14) or Monday (May 17).

Are you ok with Friday the 14th at 10am PT for a 30–45min deep dive? If not, I’ll suggest Monday.

Thanks — Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

Subject: Internal: pricing lift & recommended floor for Lumina

Internal note (do not share externally yet):

Tessa — quick margin calc based on the 500M worksheet:
- Variable cost (GPU + infra amortized, ops): ~$7–9 per 1M tokens at scale (assumes 8-bit quantized runtime and steady batching).
- SRE/Observability + retention add-on: ~$1.5 per 1M (can be waived for first 3 months as a pilot incentive).
- Target gross margin target (40–55% depending on seat of sales support): suggests a floor of ~$18–20 / 1M for committed volumes with a reasonable SLA.

Recommendation: offer an introductory committed price of $25 / 1M for the first 6 months (500M committed), include a 10% credit for overage in months 1–3, and document SLA 99.9% as the base. This keeps room for renewal discounts and still undercuts public endpoints meaningfully.

If Lumina pushes for 12mo deeper discounting we can outline a $20/1M 12mo case but require stronger commit and a longer ramp clause.

— Sergio
